abbreviations.king: R = Rex (Latin for king). CR = Charles Rex for the current monarch.
abbreviations.five: V is the Roman numeral for 5 — look for it hiding in or being removed from words.
abbreviations.service: Often means a military branch: RAF, RN (Royal Navy), RE (Royal Engineers).
abbreviations.engineers: RE = Royal Engineers. Also triggered by 'soldiers' or 'men'.
abbreviations.house: HO — standard cryptic abbreviation from Ordnance Survey maps.
abbreviations.ring: O — any round shape can indicate the letter O.
abbreviations.church: CH or CE — CE from Church of England, CH from Ordnance Survey maps.
abbreviations.tin: SN — from Latin 'stannum'. Always check periodic table symbols for elements.
abbreviations.doctor: DR, GP, MO (medical officer), or DD (doctor of divinity).
abbreviations.sailor: AB (able seaman), TAR, JACK, OS (ordinary seaman), or actual words like YACHTSMAN.
abbreviations.time: T — from physics equations like v = u + at.
abbreviations.name: N — standard abbreviation.
abbreviations.note: Musical notes: DO, RE, MI, FA, SO, LA, TI. Or individual letters A-G.
abbreviations.one: I — Roman numeral for 1. Very common in cryptic crosswords.
abbreviations.artist: RA — Royal Academy/Academician. Very common crossword abbreviation.
abbreviations.record: LP or EP — vinyl record formats. 'A record height' could be ALP (LP + A).
abbreviations.hotel: H — from the NATO phonetic alphabet (Alpha, Bravo, Charlie... Hotel).
abbreviations.fine: F — standard abbreviation, often used in anagram fodder.
abbreviations.ship: SS — as in 'on board ship' means inside SS.
abbreviations.water: C — from the Latin 'circa' or representing 'sea'.
abbreviations.alumni: OB or OBS — old boy(s), from school/university context.
abbreviations.arrived: ARR — standard abbreviation, often shortened further.
abbreviations.month: M — standard abbreviation for month or months.
abbreviations.left: L — but can also be PORT (nautical). Watch for both meanings.
abbreviations.thousand: K or M — K from kilo (informal), M from Roman numeral for 1000.
abbreviations.current: I — from Ohm's law (V = IR). Electrical current.
abbreviations.work: OP — opus, a musical work. Very common crossword abbreviation.
abbreviations.grand: G or K — G for grand (slang for £1000), K for kilo.
abbreviations.river: DEE, EXE, or just D/R — rivers often provide single letters.
abbreviations.no good: NG — a valid abbreviation, though 'good' alone can be G.
abbreviations.that is: IE — Latin 'id est'. Very common in cryptic crosswords.
abbreviations.appeal: SA — sex appeal. Where you see 'appeal' in a clue, SA is often involved.
abbreviations.second: MO — 'just a mo' means 'just a second'.
abbreviations.carelessly written: SIC — from Latin, meaning 'thus' or 'as written'. Note: s-i-c not s-i-c-k.
abbreviations.new: N — standard abbreviation. Can also be an anagram indicator.
abbreviations.operations: OPS — as in 'special ops' for special operations.
abbreviations.transport: CYCLE — a bicycle is a form of transport. Can be 'cut short' to CYC.
abbreviations.Charlie: C — from NATO phonetic alphabet. Romeo=R, Foxtrot=F, Yankee=Y, etc.
abbreviations.father: SIRE — a father or male parent. Also PA, DAD.
abbreviations.pound: L — from Latin 'libra'. A pound of weight, not money (which is also £).
abbreviations.succeeded: S — standard abbreviation for succeeded or success.
abbreviations.pass: COL — a mountain pass. Very common cryptic abbreviation.

synonyms.judge: TRY — legal sense of putting someone on trial.
synonyms.hasty: SUDDEN — if you act in a hasty way, you act suddenly.
synonyms.hearty: HALE — from the phrase 'hale and hearty'.
synonyms.when: AS — 'as I was saying' = 'when I was saying'.
synonyms.toss: ROCK — if a boat tosses, it rocks.
synonyms.poor golfer: BOGEY MAN — someone who makes lots of bogeys (one over par).
synonyms.presume: MAKE BOLD — 'to make bold' is to presume.
synonyms.touching: TACTILE — if something is touching, it's tactile.
synonyms.business: FIRM — a business is a firm.
synonyms.poorly: ILL or INFIRM — if you're poorly, you're unwell.
synonyms.smooth: SAND — to smooth something is to sand it.
synonyms.talk: RAP — informal for talk. Also where 'rap music' comes from.
synonyms.drink: PORT, GIN, RUM, ALE, SIP — common short words for drinks or drinking.
synonyms.sweet: DESSERT — your sweet course. Can be reversed in down clues.
synonyms.vessel: TUB — a small boat or container.
synonyms.lead: CONDUCT — to lead an orchestra is to conduct it. Watch for 'lead' vs 'lead' (metal).
synonyms.the fellow: HE or HIM — 'the fellow did this' = 'he did this'.
synonyms.hurry up: QUICK — 'in short, hurry up' = QUIC (quick minus K).
synonyms.height: ALP — a mountain is a height.
synonyms.told porkies: LIED — if you tell porkies (lies), you lied.
synonyms.bad feeling: RESENTMENT, ANIMUS, ENMITY — synonyms for ill will.
synonyms.prisoner: CON or LAG — short synonyms for convict/prisoner. Also POW.
synonyms.about: RE or CA (circa) — as in memo headings or approximately.
synonyms.rural community: FARM — a farm is a type of rural community.
synonyms.artificial: MADE — if something's artificial, it's man-made.
synonyms.lass: MAID — a girl or young woman. Sounds like 'made'.
synonyms.relatives: KIN — your kin are your relatives.
synonyms.briefly visits: LOOKS IN — to briefly visit is to look in.
synonyms.God in Luxor: RA or HORUS — Egyptian gods. RA is very common (2 letters).
synonyms.opening of mine: ADIT — a horizontal mine entrance. Common crossword word.
synonyms.tries: ESSAYS — to essay something is to try it.
synonyms.harassed: Anagram indicator — if letters are 'harassed', rearrange them.
synonyms.hindrance: OBSTACLE — obs (old boys) + tackle minus K.
synonyms.logical: COHESIVE — things that are logical hang together.
synonyms.bloke: COVE — old-fashioned word for a fellow or chap.
synonyms.a: PER — 'three a head' = 'three per head'. A and PER are synonymous.
synonyms.slap: EYE SHADOW — slang for makeup. Also: 'eye shadow' = one who shadows the eye (PI).
synonyms.gumshoe: PI or DI — private investigator or detective inspector.
synonyms.prepare: ARM — to arm yourself is to prepare.
synonyms.against: V or ANTI — versus or anti-.
synonyms.search: QUEST — a search is a quest.
synonyms.survivors from the past: ANTIQUES — things that survived from the past.
synonyms.decorate: TRIM — to decorate, especially a tree.
synonyms.those struggling: Anagram fodder — 'those' anagrammed gives letters to work with.
synonyms.stack: CHIMNEY or HOUSETOP — a chimney is a stack.
synonyms.squiffy: SCREWED or SLOSHED — slang for drunk/tipsy.
synonyms.satisfied: MET — if needs are satisfied, they're met.
synonyms.retire: Reversal indicator — to retire is to go back.
synonyms.master: PRO — a master is a professional.
synonyms.for the present: PRO TEM — Latin phrase meaning 'for now'.
synonyms.fate: LOT — your fate is your lot in life.
synonyms.by: TIMES — in mathematics, 'by' means 'times' (3 by 4 = 3 times 4).
synonyms.pens: SWANS — pens are female swans. Misdirection from writing implements.
synonyms.shows off: SWANKS — to show off is to swank.
synonyms.chap: MAN — a chap is a man.
synonyms.pulse: BEAN — pulses are beans/legumes. Misdirection from heartbeat.
synonyms.meaning: SENSE — 'meaning to embrace' = SENSE surrounding something.
synonyms.shrub: RUE — a type of herb/shrub. Very common 3-letter answer.
synonyms.broadcast: SOW — if you sow seeds, you broadcast/scatter them. Also AIR for TV.
synonyms.scruffy type: SCARECROW — a scarecrow is certainly a scruffy type.
synonyms.hills: DOWNS — the Surrey Downs, South Downs, etc. are hills.
synonyms.pack: FILL — to pack something is to fill it.
synonyms.egg: O — an egg is circular/oval, associated with the letter O. Also a zero score in cricket.
synonyms.bar: RAIL — a bar (as in a railing) is a rail.
synonyms.spaces: HOLES — spaces are holes. 'Spaces in women' = HOLES in WOMEN.
synonyms.healthy: WHOLESOME — spaces (HOLES) in ladies (WOMEN) minus end = WHOLESOME.
synonyms.place of business: HIVE — 'a hive of activity' is a place of business.
synonyms.secret formula: CODE — a secret formula is a code.
synonyms.tablet: E — a tablet of E (ecstasy). 'Tab of E' is common slang.
synonyms.graded: CLASSED — if you grade something, you class it.
synonyms.very behind: LAST — if you're very behind in a race, you're last.
synonyms.quizzical look: BEADY EYE — a quizzical or suspicious look.
synonyms.little jewel: BEAD — a small jewel or gem.
synonyms.you: YE — archaic form of 'you'. 'You twice' = YE + YE.
synonyms.flag: PENNON — pen (to commit to paper) + non (French refusal).
synonyms.chest of drawers: The chest OF THE DRAWER = body part (chest) + S (succeeded).
synonyms.local spirit: GENIUS LOCI — Latin for 'spirit of the place'. A local presiding deity.
synonyms.minute: Can be read as 'minute' (tiny/baby-sized) or 'minute' (60 seconds).
synonyms.inherited title: SURNAME — an inherited family name. Suriname minus I.
synonyms.small drinks: SIPS — small drinks or small amounts of liquid.
synonyms.bottles: Contains/holds — if something 'bottles' another, it contains it.

indicators.homophone: 'Heard,' 'we hear,' 'by the sounds of it,' 'in report,' 'when speaking' = find a word that sounds like another but is spelled differently.
indicators.hidden: 'In the middle of,' 'within,' 'inside,' 'some' can signal a hidden word — the answer is spelled out in consecutive letters of the clue text.
indicators.spoonerism: Swap the initial sounds of two words — 'make bold' becomes 'bake mold'.
indicators.cryptic_definition: A question mark often signals a cryptic definition — read the whole clue laterally, not as definition + wordplay.
indicators.unopened: Remove the first letter — the word hasn't been 'opened' yet.
indicators.heartless: Remove the middle letter(s) — the 'heart' of the word.
indicators.stocking: 'Stocking,' 'holding,' 'containing' = container indicator. The word 'stocks' or 'has' something inside.
indicators.embraced by: 'Embraced by,' 'seized by,' 'held by' = container indicator. Something goes inside.
indicators.surprisingly: 'Surprisingly,' 'extraordinarily,' 'oddly' = anagram indicator. Treating letters in a surprising way.
indicators.in short: 'In short,' 'briefly,' 'for short' = remove letters, usually the last one.
indicators.capsized: 'Capsized,' 'overturned,' 'flipped' = reversal indicator, especially in down clues.
indicators.back: 'Back,' 'returned,' 'reversed' = reversal indicator. In down clues, also 'up'.
indicators.keeping: 'Keeping,' 'holding,' 'containing' = container indicator. One word keeps another inside.
indicators.turning up: 'Turning up' (in down clues) = reversal indicator. Letters turn upward.
indicators.vacuous: 'Vacuous,' 'empty,' 'hollow' = remove middle letters, leaving only outer shell.
indicators.beginning: 'Beginning of,' 'opening of,' 'start of' = take the first letter.
indicators.finally: 'Finally,' 'at last,' 'in the end' = take the last letter.
indicators.cloaking: 'Cloaking,' 'covering' = take outer letters of a word (the 'cloak').
indicators.shortly: 'Shortly,' 'briefly' = abbreviated form, often remove last letter.
indicators.welcomed: 'Welcomed,' 'received,' 'taken in' = container indicator. Something is welcomed inside.
indicators.introduces: 'Introduces,' 'brings in' = container indicator or positional (puts before).
indicators.served up: 'Served up' (in down clues) = reversal indicator. Serving upward.
indicators.ultimately: 'Ultimately' = take the last letter. 'Mimosa ultimately' = A.
indicators.raised: In down clues, 'raised' = reversal indicator. Letters go upward.
indicators.wasting time: 'Wasting time' = remove T. Time = T in abbreviations.
indicators.cut short: 'Cut short' = remove the last letter(s). Truncation indicator.
indicators.well crafted: 'Well crafted,' 'crafted,' 'worked' = anagram indicator. Letters are rearranged.
indicators.revise: 'Revise,' 'revised' = anagram indicator. Revising the order of letters.
indicators.regularly: 'Regularly' = take alternate letters. Every other letter from the fodder.
indicators.at first: 'At first' = take the first letter. 'Forecaster at first' = F.
indicators.skulking indoors: 'Indoors' = WITHIN. Something skulking indoors is within.
indicators.back: 'Back' = reversal indicator. 'I pass back' = reverse I + COL = LOCI reversed.

patterns.roman_numerals: When you see numbers, try translating to Roman numerals: I=1, V=5, X=10, L=50, C=100, D=500, M=1000, K=1000 (informal).
patterns.periodic_table: Elements are often abbreviated: TIN=SN, GOLD=AU, SILVER=AG, IRON=FE, LEAD=PB, COPPER=CU.
patterns.military_services: Service often means military: RAF, RN (Royal Navy), RE (Royal Engineers), RA (Royal Artillery).
patterns.card_suits: Hearts=H, Diamonds=D, Clubs=C, Spades=S — from bridge scoring.
patterns.position_words: Words like 'behind,' 'after,' 'goes after,' 'under' (down clues) indicate letter positioning, not meaning.
patterns.question_mark: A question mark often signals wordplay in the definition itself — think laterally about the whole clue.
patterns.definition_location: The definition is almost always at the start or end of the clue — rarely in the middle.
patterns.nato_alphabet: Hotel=H, Alpha=A, Romeo=R, etc. — NATO phonetic alphabet letters appear in clues.
patterns.box_container: 'In a box,' 'boxed,' 'crated' = container indicator. Put something inside another word.
patterns.two_paths: There are two ways to arrive at cryptic answers: definition AND wordplay. If you don't know a word, the wordplay can lead you there.
patterns.hidden_reversed: Hidden words can also be reversed — look for 'back in' or similar phrases indicating a backwards hidden word.
patterns.short_drinks: Common short drink words: GIN, RUM, ALE, PORT, SIP. 'Drink' in a clue often needs a 3-4 letter word.
patterns.holy_books: Bible books make good 4-letter answers: RUTH, MARK, LUKE, JOHN, ACTS. 'Holy book' or 'book' can signal these.
patterns.egyptian_gods: Egyptian gods appear often: RA (2 letters, very common), HORUS, ISIS, OSIRIS, ANUBIS.
patterns.starting_letters: Having the starting letter is hugely valuable — think of words that fit the pattern and work backwards.
patterns.crossword_words: Some words appear mainly in crosswords: ADIT (mine entrance), ESNE (serf), ERE (before), EEL, ORE.
patterns.old_boy: OB = old boy (from school/university). 'Alumni' often signals OB or OBS.
patterns.mathematical_terms: 'By' can mean 'times' in multiplication. 'A' can mean 'per' in rates.
patterns.down_clue_reversals: In down clues, 'up,' 'served up,' 'rising,' 'climbing' = reversal (letters go upward).
patterns.misdirection_surfaces: Clues often have misleading surfaces — 'pulse' suggesting heartbeat when it means beans, 'pens' suggesting writing when it means swans.
patterns.wordplay_power: The power of wordplay: even if you don't know the answer word, the wordplay can lead you there. SERAPIS was solved purely through wordplay despite being unknown.
patterns.double_definition: Double definitions have two separate meanings with no wordplay indicators. 'Road Runner' = bird (cuckoo) AND one racing on carriageway.
patterns.pangram_awareness: Some constructors include every letter of the alphabet. If you see J, Q, or Z, watch for the other rare letters.
patterns.latin_expressions: Latin phrases appear often: SINE DIE (undated), GENIUS LOCI (spirit of place), SIC (as written).
patterns.weather_folklore: SWITHIN = Saint Swithin's Day (July 15). Folklore: if it rains, it continues 40 days. 'Supposed weather forecaster.'
patterns.egyptian_deities: SERAPIS = Greek-Egyptian god identified with Apis and Osiris. Small drinks (SIPS) bottle R, raised = SERAPIS.
patterns.war_horse: MARENGO = Napoleon's famous war horse, named after the Battle of Marengo.
patterns.canterbury_tales: The Canterbury Tales characters: The Reeve, The Pardoner, etc. 'One with a tale to tell.'
patterns.reading_both_ways: A cryptic clue has definition (start OR end) + wordplay. Determine which side is which before solving.
patterns.backwards_solving: Often solve backwards: see the answer pattern, think of words that fit, then verify the wordplay works.
